name: Bulk and cut / body recomposition
lead: Bulking and cutting is a cyclical approach to physique change: a bulk is a period of eating in a calorie surplus to gain muscle, and a cut is a period in a deficit to lose fat while keeping as much muscle as possible.[1] Body recomposition is the alternative of trying to lose fat and gain muscle at the same time.

The approach comes from bodybuilding, where most competitors build muscle through an off-season and begin cutting about 12-14 weeks before a contest.[1] In looksmaxxing communities it is debated: some advocate bulking to add size, others advocate recomposition to avoid fat gain, and some members discuss drug adjuncts. The sources reviewed contain no controlled trials of the strategies themselves.

paras: Wikipedia notes that a larger surplus or longer bulk adds more fat, and that a bigger cutting deficit speeds weight loss but raises the risk of losing muscle. It says some fat gain during bulking is expected and that whether enough lean mass can be kept during cutting to make the process worthwhile is unclear.[1]

Wikipedia distinguishes clean bulking, which aims to add muscle with little fat, takes longer and requires hitting calorie targets, from dirty bulking, an unmonitored large surplus that gives faster gains but more fat and usually needs a harsher cut.[1]

Wikipedia states that in the 1950s and 1960s nutrition for bulking up and cutting down, protein and food supplements became popular alongside bodybuilding magazines; the article does not date bulking and cutting precisely.[1]

On looksmax.org, users ask about combining weight-loss medications with bulking, and about calorie-and-macro planning for recomposition after weight loss by fasting and cardio. In one thread a poster planned alternating three-month bulks and one-month cuts to avoid getting "fluffy", and replies disagreed about whether an appetite-suppressing drug is compatible with bulking.[2] In another a user asked for tools to plan a slow recomposition to a lower body fat percentage without drugs.[3]
No studies found in the sources reviewed that evaluate bulk-and-cut cycling or recomposition. The medical papers surfaced in the research set concerned medication refill adherence and were unrelated.

timeline.event: Bodybuilding magazines popularise nutrition for bulking and cutting.[1]

lore.intro: Forum posters ask how to lean out, whether to bulk or recomp, and whether drug adjuncts help.[2][3]

claims.claim: Cycling bulks and cuts avoids getting too fat.
claims.believers: One poster planned three-month bulks with one-month cuts to avoid getting "fluffy" while lifting for appearance.[2]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that bulking adds some fat and that it is unclear whether enough lean mass can be kept during cutting to make the process worthwhile.[1]

claims.claim: An appetite-suppressing weight-loss drug can be combined with bulking for recomposition.
claims.believers: A poster said they had seen others claim the drug could be used while bulking; replies disagreed, one saying bulking on it is unlikely because it suppresses appetite.[2]
claims.experts: No published trials of this combination for bulking were found in the sources reviewed.

claims.claim: A slow recomposition with calorie and protein planning can reduce body fat while keeping muscle.
claims.believers: A poster asked for week-by-week calorie and macro plans to reach 10% body fat naturally.[3]
claims.experts: The sources reviewed contain no recomposition trials.

card.summary: Cycling calorie surplus and deficit phases to add muscle and then lean out; borrowed from bodybuilding, little direct trial evidence in the sources.
card.note: Bulking adds some fat; muscle retention during cuts is described as uncertain.

quick.overview:
Bulking means eating in a surplus to gain muscle, cutting means eating in a deficit to lose fat, and recomposition tries to do both at once. The cycle comes from bodybuilding.

On forums people debate cycle lengths and whether to recomp instead.
quick.mechanism: Calorie surplus supplies energy for muscle growth with resistance training, and a deficit draws down fat; larger surpluses add more fat and larger deficits risk muscle loss.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports that some fat gain is expected in bulks and that a large deficit raises muscle loss risk. Forum discussions of drug adjuncts are untested in the sources reviewed.
